title: Explicit Inactive Stream Reclamation With Retired Identity Protection
summary: P3E9 separates deployment identity from Observer quota and explicitly replaces fully confirmed revoked streams with bounded immutable tombstones. Offline clients never cause automatic revocation or identity reuse.
identityOwnership: server_identity owns the immutable runtime deployment pin. observer_usage owns only streams, submissions, retained bytes and tombstones. Runtime receives SELECT only on server_identity; schema-owner offline recovery alone rotates it under the existing exclusive lifecycle fence. One identity module supplies schema validation and reads to Store, Observer and recovery code.

reclamation.inspect: GET /api/v1/observer-streams/{stream}/reclamation is owner/admin read-only. A deterministic shin.observer-reclamation-plan.v1 binds deployment, stream, enrolled scope/hash and all delivery counters/retained totals. eligible requires revoked=true and confirmed_sequence=accepted_sequence. Empty revoked streams are eligible. active-stream and unconfirmed-history are explicit blocked reasons, never a TTL guess.
reclamation.apply: Administrator POST of exact {plan:<inspected plan>} to the same route validates unchanged preconditions, reserves tombstone capacity, preserves a plan/receipt tombstone, deletes confirmed retained payloads and the full stream row, decrements live registry/history quotas and appends observer.reclaimed audit in one PostgreSQL transaction. This is explicit logical data deletion, not archival durability certification or automatic vacuum.
reclamation.locks: Stream row before Observer quota row before audit-writer advisory lock, matching submission/retention order. Enrollment holds quota before admission but does not wait for an existing stream row. A concurrent reclamation waiter looks up the committed tombstone after its deleted row disappears. PostgreSQL rollback protects payload/quota/audit/tombstone consistency.
reclamation.receipt: shin.observer-reclamation-receipt.v1 binds current server_id, stream_id, plan_id, applying principal, accepted/confirmed counters and deleted row/byte counts. identity_retained=true, audit_preserved=true, source_verified=false and shared_publication_mutated=false. Only exact same-identity plan replay returns the saved receipt without new mutations; changed plans return observer-reclamation-stale.
reclamation.readAfterApply: Same-identity reclamation GET returns the saved plan for uncertain-response retry. Ordinary get/submission/confirmation/reconciliation/retention/revoke return 410 observer-stream-retired to an authorized owner/admin. Unknown or out-of-scope identities return 404. No fabricated acknowledgement or resumable response is returned for deleted evidence. The later explicit namespaceRetirement operation ends that deployment identity; it does not preserve per-stream retry receipts across the transition.
reclamation.enrollment: Tombstone lookup precedes new admission while holding quota ownership. Even changed enrollment content cannot reuse a retired stream_id within the retained deployment namespace. A fresh explicit stream/state namespace is required for normal continuation. The native Observer preserves pending state on a rejected delivery; no cursor reset or automatic repin was added. Cross-deployment identity retirement follows the separately confirmed namespaceRetirement contract, never an ordinary enrollment request.
reclamation.audit: Migration 011 removes only the historical audit-to-stream FK, retaining the original identifiers, audit rows and existing project/workspace constraints. The current API never uses audit as an editable stream registry. Audit export/retention remains its own explicit policy.

bounds.saturation: At tombstone capacity, apply returns observer-tombstone-capacity without deleting anything. Exact already-applied replay still works. These explicit logical caps are not a total PostgreSQL disk bound; audit and MVCC/vacuum have separate lifetimes.
bounds.noExpiry: No timer, LRU, ordinary recovery or live reclamation deletes tombstones. The explicit offline namespaceRetirement successor rotates the deployment pin atomically with bounded tombstone deletion; unchanged old HTTP requests and native queues cannot join the new namespace. Saturation never invokes it automatically.
bounds.pending: Ordinary reclamation still rejects revoked unconfirmed streams. Dev34 adds only the separate explicit administrator unconfirmedDiscard contract above; it does not certify an archive, bypass tombstone capacity or reclaim long-offline non-revoked streams.

recovery: Ordinary recovery plan/receipt remain shin.server-recovery-plan.v2 and shin.server-recovery-receipt.v2. Plans bind up to4096 tombstone identities and SHA256 digests of their saved metadata; receipts report retained_tombstones. Ordinary recovery preserves all tombstones and fences old reclamation plans. The separate dev35 namespaceRetirement commands have their own request/plan/receipt schemas and explicit discard confirmation; both reuse the bounded latest maintenance slot. No old-plan execution compatibility reader or automatic downgrade.
migration: Explicit SQL 011 preserves prior deployment identity, full streams, receipts, audit and last recovery evidence; moves server_id out of observer_usage; creates an empty immutable-runtime tombstone table and zero quota. Checksums 001..010 stay unchanged. Normal reads do not migrate. No Observer local schema or actor-worker/SLJS protocol changes.
sourceUse: PostgreSQL row-lock wait/transaction semantics and historical FK ownership informed the design. Built-in SHA256 over UTF8 JSON text avoids adding an extension to hash retained recovery metadata; hashes are not authentication or backup proof.
